title: Adjacency rejects distinct inputs
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let $n,s$ be natural numbers. Let $x$ and $x'$ be distinct Boolean inputs, each of length $n$, and let $c$ and $c'$ be arbitrary configurations of $M$ on inputs $x$ and $x'$, respectively. The adjacency formula evaluated on the concatenation of their Boolean codes is false.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols
replaced:
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let
$n,s\in\mathbb{N}$. If $x$ and $x'$ are distinct Boolean inputs, both of length $n$,
then for any configurations $c$ of $M$ on input $x$ and $c'$ of $M$ on input $x'$, the
adjacency formula evaluated on the concatenation of their Boolean codes is false.
